etymologies.etymologyHTML: From order +‎ -ly.

definitions.definition: Being on duty; keeping order; conveying orders.

quote.citation: 1814 July 7, [Walter Scott], Waverley; or, ’Tis Sixty Years Since. […], volume (please specify |volume=I to III), Edinburgh:  […] James Ballantyne and Co. for Archibald Constable and Co.; London: Longman, Hurst, Rees, Orme, and Brown, →OCLC:

definitions.definition: A hospital attendant given a variety of non-medical duties.
(military) A soldier who carries out minor tasks for a superior officer.
(now rare) According to good order or practice; appropriately, in a well-behaved or orderly (adjective) way. [from 15th c.]

quote.citation: c. 1590–1592 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Taming of the Shrew”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act II, scene ii]:
quote.text: You are blunt; go to it orderly.

quote.citation: 1991, Chor-San Heng Khoo, Physics of Liquid Crystalline Materials, CRC Press, →ISBN, page 33:
quote.text: Phase R: the rods are linked three by three and form planar twodimensional hexagonal networks. In both cases, the networks are orderly stacked in a three-dimensional lattice.

quote.citation: 2014, Huei-Huang Lee, Finite Element Simulations with ANSYS Workbench 15: Theory, Applications, Case Studies, SDC Publications, →ISBN, page 191:
quote.text: The rectangles are orderly stacked with the topmost rectangle representing the most visible entity and subsequent rectangles representing entities underneath the mouse cursor, front to back.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) In order; in a particular order or succession; with a suitable arrangement. [15th–19th c.]

quote.citation: 1567, Ovid, translated by Arthur Golding, Metamorphoses, section I:
quote.text: The earth from heaven, the sea from earth, he parted orderly, / And from the thicke and foggie ayre, he tooke the lightsome skie.

quote.citation: 1603, Michel de Montaigne, chapter 12, in John Florio, transl., The Essayes […], book II, London:  […]  Val[entine] Simmes for Edward Blount […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Thus orderly marshaled, they take their course and swim whither their journey tends, as broad and wide behind as before […].

quote.citation: 1624, John Smith, Generall Historie, Kupperman, published 1988, page 149:
quote.text: And in the Tombe which is an arch made of mats, they lay them orderly.
